full_dataset_size: Repo total ~7.8 MB: hotel-history.json 3.1 MB + hotels.geojson 2.3 MB + TSV 0.4 MB are the whole committed data; everything is in this sample (only owner-contact columns removed). Raw per-period Comptroller CSVs (data/periods/: 2023, 2024Q2-2025Q4 quarterly, 2026-JAN..MAY monthly; ~5k rows each) are gitignored and NOT in the repo; they come from the Texas Comptroller Hotel Occupancy Tax public-data quarterly download (form-driven query, all quarters back to 2000s available, ~10 MB per quarter statewide).
description: Property-grain Texas hotel room-revenue history derived from Texas Comptroller hotel occupancy tax (HOT) filings: for 5,141 Texas hotels (name, address, rooms, lat/lng) the repo holds taxable room revenue per period (2023 annual, 2024Q2-2026Q1 quarterly, Apr-May 2026 monthly) and a per-night RevPAR computed as revenue/rooms/days, plus a 767-row STR/CoStar-style property list (brand, chain scale, class, submarket) merged onto part of the panel. Source is the author's export of the Comptroller's public HOT quarterly data (raw files gitignored); the committed JSON/GeoJSON are the build outputs. For ABNB this is a state-level hotel demand/pricing benchmark (gap #8): aggregate revenue by quarter/submarket gives Texas hotel revenue growth and RevPAR by market and chain scale through May 2026, comparable against Inside Airbnb Austin/Texas STR supply and the NA nights/ADR path; the parsing method transfers to the Comptroller's own quarterly downloads for a 20-year history.
issues: No LICENSE file in the repo (author's build output; Comptroller HOT data itself is public record). data/box/texas-hospitality.tsv is an STR/CoStar-style property export (columns 'Data Participation', chain scale, FEMA fields) whose redistribution terms are unknown -- owner name/phone/contact columns were dropped from the saved samples, and a human should decide before quoting the STR fields; that TSV also has a repeated header row inside it so a few rows parse misaligned. Room counts come from the Comptroller filing (1-room placeholder filings exist; author filters rooms<2 and RevPAR>$2000). Revenue is taxable room revenue, not total; hotels matched across periods by normalised address, so renamed/re-permitted properties break the series. 2026Q2 is partial (Apr+May). The Socrata datasets on data.texas.gov (ids vmy5-jctb, ifh4-9tpn, er34-v24h, qik7-ypfg, 9xry-ncut, hdzd-884n) are local-HOT city-level reporting and permits, not this property-grain series; the property-grain source is the Comptroller's form-driven HOT public data query, which was not run here.
geography: Texas, USA (statewide, property-level with lat/lng; markets Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, El Paso, etc.)
